title: Non-fiction text features
examples: What are headings used for in a book?
How do captions help me understand pictures?
Why does the writer make some words bold?

explain.say: Today we will learn about text features in non-fiction writing. These features help you understand the text better. Let us start by looking at headings.
A heading is a short title for a section of writing. It tells you what the next part will be about. For example, a heading might say 'Types of Rainforest Animals'.
Next we look at captions. A caption is a short description under a picture. It explains what the picture shows to the reader. For instance, a caption might say 'A monkey eating a banana'.

Bold text is another feature we see often. Writers use bold text to show important words. It helps your eyes see the most important information quickly. For example, the word 'mammal' might be bolded.

These features all work together to help you read non-fiction. They guide your reading and help you remember key facts. For example, a heading might be 'Ocean Life', a picture might have a caption, and the word 'coral' might be bolded.
In real life, you see these features everywhere. Think about a recipe book. The heading might be 'Making Pancakes', the picture might have a caption, and the ingredient 'flour' might be bolded.

faq.q: What is the difference between a heading and a subheading?
faq.a: A heading is a main title for a big section. A subheading is a smaller title that divides a section into smaller parts. You can also ask, 'Are they the same thing?' or 'What is a section title?'

faq.q: Can I tell what a caption is just by looking at it?
faq.a: Captions are always placed right near the picture they describe. They give extra details about what you are seeing. You might also ask, 'Where do captions go?' or 'What does a picture description look like?'
asks: What does a picture description look like?

faq.q: Why do writers use bold text so much?
faq.a: Writers use bold text to make sure you notice the most important words. It helps you remember the key vocabulary. You could also ask, 'Why are some words dark?' or 'What is the purpose of bolding?'
asks: What is the purpose of bolding?

faq.q: Do I need to know all these features to read well?
faq.a: No, but knowing them helps you understand the text faster. They give you a map of what the writer is saying. You might also ask, 'Are these helpful for reading?' or 'Do I need to learn these?'
asks: Do I need to learn these?

faq.q: If I see a lot of headings, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means the writer has organized the information into many smaller topics. This makes the long text easier to read and follow. You could also ask, 'Is the text organized?' or 'Are there many topics?'

facts: Headings give a general idea of the section.
Bold text draws attention to key vocabulary.
These features make non-fiction easier to read.

quiz.say: A title above a section that tells you the topic is a:
quiz.why: A heading acts like a signpost, telling you the topic ahead.

wrong.0: A paragraph is a group of sentences, not a title.
wrong.2: A caption goes under a picture, not above a section.
wrong.3: Bold text only highlights a single important word.

quiz.say: What is the purpose of a caption under a diagram?

options.show: To make the writing look pretty
options.say: To make the writing look pretty

quiz.why: The caption gives necessary details about the visual information.

wrong.1: Summaries are usually at the end of a section.
wrong.2: Captions support the text, they do not replace it.
wrong.3: Appearance is not the main job of a caption.

quiz.say: If a writer wants you to remember the word 'photosynthesis', they might:

options.show: Write it in all capital letters
options.say: Write it in all capital letters

quiz.why: Bold text is the standard way to emphasize key vocabulary.

wrong.0: Small fonts make important words hard to spot.
wrong.2: All caps can be hard to read and look like shouting.
wrong.3: Italics are often used for titles, not just emphasis.
